recipes.name: Camp Cornbread
ingredients_raw: 1 (8 ounce) package corn bread muffin mix

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13 inch baking pan.
Place the muffin mix a large mixing bowl. Stir in the milk and egg. Mix in the cream corn and sugar. Pour batter into prepared pan.
Bake in preheated oven for 30 minutes, or until a knife inserted into the center of pan comes out clean.

raw_recipe.headline: Camp Cornbread
raw_recipe.description: Cream-style corn is added to corn muffin mix, making this recipe easy as well as portable.

review.reviewBody: Not at all like traditional cornbread. Very moist and sweet. My husband says its like the cornbread side they serve at Chevy's Fresh Mex. We liked it with honey butter.

I made this recipe, and it came out so good! Following advice of other reviews, I did not use any sugar at all, as I agree the cream corn is sweet enough already, I did use (2) 8.5 oz boxes of Jiffy mix, but I used one original and one honey as that is what I had on hand, So, I'm not sure if that made it any sweeter or not, (I didn't think it was too sweet if it did.) and doubled everything else, except creamed corn (14.5 oz. can). Baked at 375 for about 20 min, in an 8x8 (also per other reviews) but next time might try doing 30 instead. Will make again for sure.

Made for a Thanksgiving party of 28 people. I made some minor modifications, only added approx 3tbs of white ssugar instead of the 1 cup in the recipe and added in approx 1 cup of marshmallows in with the pecans to the topping
I also baked mine in my crock from my slow cooker, that way I could put the crock into the slow cooker on low (or warm if your slow cooker has that setting) to keep warm.
It was a hit!!!

5 stars when after I changed it up a little. My version tasted wonderful and moist. I used Jiffy corn bread mix, which is sweet enough NO sugar needed, added 1 small diced onion about 3/4 cup and 1/2 cup of diced green bell peppers, 1/2 cup shredded cheddar cheese, and the rest of the listed ingredients except sugar. Baked at 400 for 15-20 minutes in a sprayed 8x8 glass pan. Came out perfect tasted wonderful with 13 bean spicy soup. I usually always change recipes to suit my southern taste and I've never had a complaint. :) Happy cooking everyone.

This turned out great. I usually make Paula Dene’s corn casserole, but didn’t have sour cream so tried this recipe out instead. I made them in a mini cupcake tray for bite sized goodness. I didn’t add any sugar and added a little butter. They were also really good when I reheated in my air fryer for extra crunchy crust.

I've been making my own version of this recipe 20yrs or so, it is the best. The creamed corn gives it its moistness and it pairs well with many dishes or simply by its self with only drizzled honey or strawberry jam. I am a southern cook, taught by many great southern cooks throughout my life so giving my 2 cents of advice ...
to achieve the thickness/height,definitely use 2 boxes of Jiffy yellow mix doubling the recipe. also ,using a cast iron pan is ideal...greased &heated before you pour in your batter then immediately into the oven , gives it a nice crisp edge. I like to put a few tablespoons of real butter as well and brush the top with butter after its done. The sugar issue here...wow...is not necessary. The yellow cornbread mix and creamed corn already has a sweetness to it but if you feel the need, only a couple teaspoons of sugar will achieve more sweetness. Remember...this is cornbread , not cake. Enjoy everyone and Happy New Year??

I made it in a preheated cast iron skillet for a crispy brown bottom. Just a tablespoon of cooking oil to coat the preheated skillet. I also add a good squirt of sour cream (prob ~1 1/2 T) for a hint of tang. The family loved it!!

Exactly what I was looking for, but it was too thin!
DON'T USE 9x12 pan! It would be thin as a pancake!
Use 8X8 and it should turn out thick enough to cut for buttering! I might try for muffins next time and even add jalapenos on top.

Very easy and delicious, but I am only giving 4 stars instead of 5 because the instructions are a little off. I only used 1/4 cup of sugar, as others suggested, and this was more than enough. I cannot imagine how it would taste with the full 1/2 cup. I made muffins (I ended up with 9), but they did not rise at all - therfore, I think it would be too flat if made in a 9x13 pan. I will definitely make again, but with less sugar, and a muffin tin or 8x8 pan.

I make basically the same thing, except I omit the white sugar and only add a little milk if needed. The creamed corn seems to be enough of a liquid. After mixing, I layer batter in a square 9" pan, put a layer of shredded cheddar cheese, then more batter, more cheese and crumbled cooked bacon. That, with a bowl of chili can't be beat! SWEETIE 2-4

I made this without adding the sugar and it was great and plenty sweet. Jiffy mix has sugar in it and creamed corn has sugar in it. save your waistline and leave it out. I made this in a hot buttered 10" cast iron skillet at 350 for 20 minutes and it was perfect.

It was simple to make. I made muffins and followed the directions as posted. It was almost sickening sweet. If I had read the reviews prior to making it I would have left the sugar completely out. Maybe I’ll try it again and follow some of the suggestions in the reviews. There are too many good cornbread recipes out there not to use instead. I just tried this one due to its simplicity.

I have been adding canned corn to corn bread recipes for years. I tried adding 1/2 the sugar and is was still very sweet. It was like dessert when the kids added their Jelly, Lol. I was good, just too sweet for my taste. It was not necessary to make it taste good.. If you double the recipe, as I always do, try 3 eggs instead of two, Even better as it stay moist longer. Thanks for sharing!
Made without an egg (none available that day). Turns out I liked it even better.

Really great! I didn't have the same size can of creamed corn so I just measured one cup, 8 oz. I did not add the sugar and it really didn't have to have it in my opinion. I made muffins also. This was fantastic!
This was a yummy, moist cornbread which was easy to make. So glad I found this recipe!
Best ever
Love it! Added chopped jalapeños!
Easy yet delicious!!! A definite keeper!
I eliminated the sugar all together. It was plenty sweet and super moist without it!
